strengths: The validate hardening is a textbook extension: checkTaskReportAudit sits beside the existing shape checks as one documented single-purpose function (tools/kb.mjs:786-812), its messages keep the usage-error voice, and its doc comment's flow claim was made true before it shipped — the r0 review forced the retrieval protocol to migrate (audit, fill, validate once) instead of special-casing the draft, which is quality.no-compat-softening applied to a process flow.

Two-sided test evidence: three natural REDs for the new rejections, three disclosed mutation proofs for the acceptance guards, and the twelfth-cell pin whose comment names the exact reordering hazard it guards (tests/kb.test.mjs:2200-2204). All six new tests mint scratch state through makeRepo -> scratchDir (tests/kb.test.mjs:147-148).

The review loop enforced this batch's own new rules on this batch: both T1 fix-round audits reproduced byte for byte in r2, and the T2 r1 reviewer applied the just-shipped item 6 to its own verdict (four findings, four fix_rounds entries, one for one) and traced every refreshed report value to a recorded run.

The seventh eval record is honest about what held: the doctored seeded report passes the hardened validate by design, and the record's notes say so, crediting the reviewer's row arithmetic as the gate — no over-claiming, per knowledge-base.state-only-the-source, in the very file that certifies the templates.

All four changed template/root pairs share one blob id at HEAD (kb.mjs c1dcfc4c, implementer.md 568f398c, task-reviewer.md ebcc6a65, orchestrating SKILL a944598a), render --check is up to date, and T2's live-run greps prove a fresh init ships all four sentences with no repo-local token.

The interleaved owner commit was contained cleanly: e4e0968 secured verbatim as its own docs(readme) commit, two style notes surfaced to the owner instead of silently edited, and the ledger corrected its own range-containment slip in writing (progress.md line 6).

Gates all green at HEAD: 200/200 tests with ~99% statement coverage, kb and backlog checks ok, a linear eight-commit range with clean Conventional Commits, and all eleven workspace deliverables validate under the hardened gate they themselves introduced.

No entry covers securing owner content found mid-batch: the controller improvised correctly (verbatim own commit e4e0968, two style notes surfaced instead of edited, kept outside every task range), but the ledger first misstated which task range contained the commit and needed a written correction (progress.md line 6). The procedure currently lives only in batch 14's ledger, which does not survive compaction.

entry.summary: Owner content found uncommitted on the shared tree mid-batch: commit it verbatim as its own commit at once, surface concerns to the owner instead of editing, and record its exact position relative to task ranges in the ledger.
body: Batch 14: the README convergence paragraphs surfaced while T1 ran; secured as their own docs(readme) commit (e4e0968), two notes surfaced to the owner (a dropped link, lowercase product names), nothing silently changed.

Verify the interleave position with git log before writing the ledger line: state which task commits sit below and above it. A wrong containment claim forces a ledger correction and changes which range the task review must read (batch 14, T1).
At aggregation the commit stays its own commit; no task diff absorbs it, and the task-review dispatch names it as owner content to be judged as such.

template_defects.what: The new gate inspects only the top-level self_audit, so a fix-round audit recorded without --report — the batch 12 shape this batch set out to remove — still validates. It recurred inside this very batch (T1 fix round 0, skipped 3) and cost the r1-to-r2 round; only the task reviewer caught it.
template_defects.fix: Extend checkTaskReportAudit to scan fix_rounds[].tests[].output for an audit summary carrying a nonzero "skipped" (the transcript is JSON, the pattern is narrow and did not occur in any legitimate output this batch), or explicitly keep it judged by adding the check to the task-reviewer's numbered list; if neither, file the backlog item.

template_defects.what: The verbatim-output invariant governs tests, live_run, and fix_rounds[].tests but sits inside live_run's parenthetical; a reader of the tests bullet alone never sees it, and the T2 r1 reviewer had to spend a considered-and-cleared cycle on the placement.
template_defects.fix: At the next template-touching batch, lift the clause onto its own line above the field list, wording unchanged; bundle it there so it shares that batch's evals rerun instead of costing its own.

assessment.text: The branch delivers the spec exactly: the hardened validate with its twelve-cell state space pinned, the four template sentences plus the rebuild step, and the seventh eval record keyed to both changed template blobs — verified equal to git rev-parse at 508a089, so the evals debt both tasks disclosed is paid. The one wording deviation (item 6 grew a second, disposition sentence) came from a review finding and is justified. The branch audit at HEAD is clean: 10 deterministic rows pass with 0 skipped, and all 28 judged rows pass over the whole diff. The internal loop already enforced this batch's own new rules on this batch — reproduced audits, one-for-one findings lists, traced report values — and all eleven workspace deliverables validate under the gate the batch introduced. 200/200 tests, kb and backlog checks ok, render drift-free, eval worktree removed, linear range with the owner's verbatim README commit correctly contained outside every task diff. No issues to file; the retrospective carries two ready knowledge edits, one new procedure entry, and two template defects for the next template-touching batch. Ready to finish: fetch, rebase onto main, re-run the gates, ff-only merge, tick HR-041/043/050.
